evidence.text: Q3 jet fuel ran well above the price Alaska guided on. The July guide assumed $3.75/gal economic fuel (July $3.60, August-September at the $3.85 spot curve). The EIA US Gulf Coast jet spot then averaged about $3.71 in August and about $4.38 in September, against roughly $3.2-3.3 in early July. That points to Q3 economic fuel of roughly $4.0-4.1. Alaska is unhedged (it exited its hedging program) and its CFO said at the investor day that '$0.10 is, for us, $120 million' a year. A $0.25-0.35/gal overrun is therefore about $75-105M pretax, or about $0.45-0.60 per share after the 35% tax rate on 113.5M shares. That puts the quarter near the bottom of the $0.00-1.00 guide and below EW's $0.35 consensus unless revenue makes up the gap.

July 2026 beat on EPS (-0.92 vs -0.98) and still fell 2.4%; April 2026, when guidance was suspended on fuel, fell 4.8%. Peer analog: Delta's Q3 fuel came in at $3.61 against a $3.15 July assumption, EPS was $1.72 against a $2.00-2.50 guide, and DAL fell only about 3% on 2026-10-09.

Had it been fully priced, consensus would be near zero. Partly priced: the stock is down 17.6% in 20 sessions, and the fuel series is public to anyone.

evidence.text: RVIA wholesale shipments for WGO's fiscal Q4 (Jun-Aug 2026) were down about 14% in towables and about 13% in motorhomes. Towables: Jun 22,728 (-14.3%), Jul 17,754 (-9.8%), Aug 20,790 (-16.9%). Motorhomes: Jun 2,756 (-1.6%), Jul 2,194 (-25.6%), Aug 2,809 (-11.7%). Motorhomes (46% of WGO's 9M revenue and its only growth segment, +17% YoY in 9M) turned sharply negative, against a hard comparison of Q4 FY25 motorhome revenue of $361.2M (+17.3%). Applying these rates to the Q4 FY25 segment base (towable $306M, motorhome $361M, marine $95M), plus WGO's towable share loss (Q3 units -26.5% against an industry of about -17%), gives about $645-655M. That is roughly 1-2% under the ~$660M consensus but inside the company's own 'down double digits' guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-06-25): revenue $698.7M against ~$777M consensus (-10%) plus a guide cut, and the stock rose +13.24%. Q4 FY25 (2025-10-22): revenue beat ($777M against $744M) plus the first FY26 guide, +28.53%. Revenue misses have not been punished on this name lately.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $660M sits above the guide midpoint ($641M) despite three months of industry data released after the June guide. If the market had marked revenue to the shipment series, the published revenue consensus would sit nearer $645M. Against that, the stock is -20% in 20 sessions with put skew, so the price may already embed it even if the published consensus does not.
evidence.independence: July and June data come from separate RVIA releases (https://rv-pro.com/news/july-wholesale-shipments-near-20k-units-down-11-9-from-2025/, 2026-08-25; https://rv-pro.com/news/rvia-june-rv-shipments-down-13-1-yoy/). Camping World Q2 (2026-07-29) had same-store new units -16.3% and expected July to be 'more acute' (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729469894/en/). It is an industry proxy, not WGO's own number, and Class B vans (WGO's strength) were +19.5% in June, which partly offsets.

evidence.text: The RVIA fall RoadSigns forecast (published 2026-10-16) cut calendar-2026 wholesale shipments to ~290,000 (range 284,600-295,400, from a 314k median in the summer edition and 349k in spring). That is at the very bottom of WGO's own CY26 assumption of 290-310k. It projects CY2027 'relatively flat' at ~285,000 (274,700-295,300), with year-over-year growth only in H2 2027. WGO's first FY27 guide tomorrow will be built on that industry base, so it likely implies flat-to-down revenue from ~$2.65-2.70B, with any EPS growth coming from footprint and cost actions rather than volume.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: First full-year guide in October 2025 (FY26 adj EPS $2.00-2.70 against $2.24 consensus): +28.53%. Guide cut in June 2026 (to $1.65-2.00 against ~$2.27 consensus): +13.24% (relief). Guidance changes move this stock a lot and not always in the direction of the number.
evidence.why_not_priced: Published four sessions before the print and two days after Citi's cut. If FY27 estimates were already marked to a flat 285k industry, the published FY27 consensus would be near FY26's ~$1.75-1.80 rather than the $2.99 still visible on aggregators. But the street FY27 bar is unsourced, and the stock's 20-day drop plus put skew suggest much of this is in the price, so the finding is capped small.
evidence.independence: Thor (2026-09-22) deferred FY27 guidance, expects 'relatively flat' retail and still says it can 'materially improve its earnings profile' through >$100M of cost actions (https://rv-pro.com/news/thors-q4-fiscal-2026-more-challenging-than-anticipated/). That cuts both ways: WGO also has footprint actions with 'benefits expected in fiscal 2027' (Q3 release).

evidence.text: Thor's quarter to 31 July 2026 (overlapping two of WGO's three Q4 months) had North American Motorized gross margin down 600bp on units -13.1%, 'higher promotional activity' in both towables and motorized, and fifth-wheel units -34.7%. Fifth wheels are Grand Design's core, and WGO management singled them out as under 'targeted pressure'. WGO guided Q4 gross and EBITDA margins 'slightly lower sequentially but flattish to last year' (Q4 FY25 adj EBITDA $38.2M, 4.9%). Thor's read-through puts that margin guide at risk, especially in towables. Net of the rest of the company, WGO's motorhome segment starts from a near-zero margin in Q4 FY25 (-0.1%), so its year-over-year comparison is easy.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26: gross margin 13.6% against 13.7% (flat) with an EPS miss of $0.66 against $0.82, and the stock rose +13.2%. Margin disappointment has not been the line this stock sold on recently.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS at $0.47 already sits below the ~$0.52 guide midpoint, so part of this is in the bar. What would show it fully priced is consensus nearer the bottom of the guide ($0.34-0.40). The peer print is a month old and the stock has fallen since, so most of it is likely priced.
evidence.independence: The Thor 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000730263/000073026326000028/thoq4fy26-earningsrelease.htm) is the same underlying document as the RV PRO write-up. evidence.text: On 2026-08-20 WGO entered a Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement with JPMorgan as agent. It extends the up-to-$350M asset-based revolver to 2031-08-20 at SOFR +1.25-1.75%, and it is undrawn. Together with the $100M note redemption already done in FY26 (long-term debt $442.9M against $540.5M at FY25 year-end), the money buys liquidity and maturity runway, not a ramp or distress. Management also guided a further working-capital release in Q4, so Q4 cash flow could fund debt reduction or support the dividend.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on financing. Net leverage of 3.0x (Q3) was flagged on the call as the balance-sheet priority.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public for two months. The only unpriced piece is the Q4 cash-flow and leverage print, which would show up as a lower net-leverage figure in the release. It is small.
evidence.independence: 10-Q for Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000107687/000162828026045496/wgo-20260530.htm): ABL undrawn, debt $450M gross. Shares the 8-K's subject matter but is a separate document.

evidence.text: The Q3 10-Q states WGO 'will perform a quantitative impairment assessment of the Chris-Craft trade name' in Q4 FY26 and warns of a possible charge (indefinite-lived trade names $352.3M in total, Marine goodwill $136.1M). A charge would hit reported EPS (excluded from adjusted) and is not quantified anywhere.

evidence.why_not_priced: No preview mentions a charge, and reported-EPS estimates are not set to absorb one. If priced, reported-EPS consensus would sit well below adjusted. It is a non-cash item below operating income and is usually looked through, so it is filed at a fraction of its dollars.
